stories.title: Military police stop accepting sexual-offence complaints; Bill C-11 strips CAF jurisdiction
stories.summary: As of June 15, 2026 Canadian Forces military police were directed to stop accepting Criminal Code sexual-offence complaints, ahead of passage of the Liberal government's military-justice reform bill (Bill C-11), which carries Louise Arbour's recommendation to remove the CAF's power to investigate and prosecute sexual offences. Civilian police and Crowns take over; 140+ existing CFNIS investigations are expected to be transferred. The federal government is, in effect, conceding that military jurisdiction over sexual offences is structurally broken. Standing item carried forward from the morning brief; no new public reporting in the evening window.

The jurisdiction handover vindicates the personal CFNIS prosecution filings at E:\legal\ and pairs with the Jan 2026 ONSC stay (military police evidence-tampering). stories.title: Youth and environmental groups sue Carney government over climate rollbacks
stories.summary: Three young people and two environmental groups filed suit in Federal Court alleging the Carney government is undoing Canada's climate plan and breaking federal law in the process. They ask the court to order Ottawa to develop a climate plan that achieves Canada's legally binding 2030 targets. The suit lands as Trudeau-era climate architects (McKenna, Guilbeault, Wilkinson) are sidelined and former environment minister Steven Guilbeault exits politics amid a public split with Carney over the change in course.
stories.connection: NEW executive-accountability thread: a statutory-duty challenge to a sitting PM over missed legally binding targets is squarely on-mission for the accountability investigation (governance / rule-of-law failure pattern). Recommend opening a climate_accountability or governance_litigation tracker and cross-referencing revolving_door_analysis.json (Brookfield-energy / Carney) and the Guilbeault resignation. stories.title: Alberta First Nations chiefs ask RCMP to examine Smith referendum as possible 'treason'
stories.summary: Chiefs representing First Nations across Alberta have asked the RCMP to look into whether Premier Danielle Smith's upcoming fall sovereignty referendum amounts to criminal treason, arguing it threatens treaty rights and the constitutional order. Smith publicly told the chiefs to 'check themselves' over the accusations. A federal-provincial / Crown-Indigenous constitutional confrontation with a criminal-law overlay.

stories.title: StatCan confirms Q1 2026 population fell 55,025 on ~20% fewer immigrants
stories.summary: Statistics Canada confirmed the national population declined by 55,025 in Q1 2026, to an estimated 41,417,056 as of April 1 -- the first decline of the immigration-driven era. Permanent immigration fell ~20% year-over-year, to 83,149 from 104,210 in Q1 2025. The drop intersects reduced immigration targets and temporary-foreign-worker policy already under accountability review.
stories.connection: Macro context for tfw_abuse_analysis.json and immigration-policy threads; tracks demographic pressure underlying labour-market and housing narratives. Now confirmed with the immigrant-volume breakdown beyond the morning brief.

stories.title: Manitoba hepatitis A outbreak prompts U.S. CDC travel advisory
stories.summary: A hepatitis A outbreak in Manitoba has produced 165 hospitalizations, including eight ICU admissions and four deaths, prompting the U.S. CDC to issue a travel advisory for the province. A foreign public-health advisory against a Canadian jurisdiction is a notable public-health-governance signal.
